findings.message: references 2 known high-risk or anonymous destination(s)
findings.remediation: Route all network traffic through allowlisted, authenticated endpoints only.
findings.impact: Requests to anonymous or high-risk destinations can disclose plugin data to an untrusted operator.
findings.attack_vector: Network URL matches a known paste, tunnel, webhook, or anonymous file-hosting service.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Remove embedded credentials, rotate exposed secrets, and load them only from a protected secret store.
findings.impact: Hardcoded API keys/tokens can be exfiltrated by anyone with read access to the plugin source.
findings.attack_vector: Secret key pattern matched in source — key is shipped in plaintext to all consumers.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: downloads and pipes code directly to interpreter
findings.remediation: Do not execute code downloaded at runtime; pin and review shipped code.
findings.impact: Downloading and piping remote code to an interpreter gives attackers full RCE on the CI runner.
findings.attack_vector: curl/wget output piped to bash/node/python — no checksum verification on fetched content.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: references an operating-system persistence mechanism (3 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Document and require explicit user approval for persistent operating-system changes.
findings.impact: Lifecycle hooks (install/uninstall/activate) create persistence — malicious code runs across sessions.
findings.attack_vector: Plugin registers install/activate handlers that modify the host environment on load.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: writes to system directories or boot locations
findings.remediation: Restrict file writes to user-owned directories with explicit approval.
findings.impact: Writing to system directories or boot locations gives attackers persistent root-level access.
findings.attack_vector: File write to /etc/init.d, /Library/LaunchDaemons, or Program Files — survives reboots.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: disables TLS verification or references plaintext HTTP transport
findings.remediation: Use HTTPS and keep TLS certificate verification enabled.
findings.impact: Disabling TLS verification or using plaintext HTTP allows MITM interception of all traffic.
findings.attack_vector: rejectUnauthorized: false or http:// URL — attacker can intercept/modify all requests.
